title: @object-ui/components ships dist/index.d.ts with extensionless relative re-exports, so any consumer on moduleResolution nodenext sees every named export as missing
body:
Found while clearing the six small packages of #5214. Not fixed there: it is a different artifact (`.d.ts`, not `.js`), in a package outside that card's file surface, and no gate covers it today.

## What was measured, 2026-08-20, on a full build

`packages/components/dist/index.d.ts` re-exports through **extensionless relative specifiers**:

```
export { cn } from './lib/utils';
export { getLazyIcon, isLucideIconName, LazyIcon, toKebabIconName } from './lib/lazy-icon';
export { hasDeclaredVisibilityGate } from './renderers/action/visibility-gate';
export * from './ui';
...
```

21 such re-exports in that one file. TypeScript under `"moduleResolution": "nodenext"` (or `node16`) does not extension-search them either, so it cannot follow any of them, and every symbol they carry reads as absent from the package.

## How it shows up

Adding the #5214 / #4538 step-2 pin to `packages/fields/tsconfig.json` — the same two lines `packages/react` already carries — turns `tsc` red with a flood of TS2305 that has nothing to do with `fields`:

```
src/index.tsx(13,10): error TS2305: Module '"@object-ui/components"' has no exported member 'Badge'.
src/index.tsx(13,17): error TS2305: Module '"@object-ui/components"' has no exported member 'Avatar'.
src/widgets/AddressField.tsx(2,10): error TS2305: Module '"@object-ui/components"' has no exported member 'Input'.
src/widgets/BooleanField.tsx(2,10): error TS2305: Module '"@object-ui/components"' has no exported member 'Switch'.
... (every named import from @object-ui/components, across the package)
```

The exports are all really there; TypeScript just cannot reach them through the extensionless hops.

## Why it is invisible today

`@object-ui/components` builds through vite, so `pnpm check:esm-specifiers` correctly judges it **not** specifier-preserving and never scans it — that verdict is about the emitted `.js`, which vite does resolve. The typings are emitted by a different half of the same build and carry the defect that the `.js` does not. `pnpm check:node-esm-load` only ever `import()`s the runtime entry, so it never exercises type resolution at all. Every gate in the repository is green in this state.

The consequence is scoped but real: **`@object-ui/components` is the blocker for pinning `nodenext` anywhere downstream of it.** Five packages took the pin in the #5214 work (`auth`, `mobile`, `collaboration`, `permissions`, `providers` — none of them import `@object-ui/components`); `fields` could not, and it is the largest of the six. Any future package that wants the compiler to enforce its extensions hits this same wall.

## Suggested shape

Two independent questions, worth separating before anyone writes code:

1. Should the emitted `.d.ts` carry explicit extensions? If yes, this is a `vite-plugin-dts` / `unplugin-dts` configuration question in `packages/components`, not a source edit — the source specifiers are resolved away in the `.js` and only survive into the typings.
2. Should a gate see it? The existing specifier leg deliberately scopes itself to specifier-preserving **`.js`** builds. A typings-level criterion would be a third leg with its own size assertion, not a widening of leg 1 — the header of `scripts/check-node-esm-load.mjs` argues at length for why each leg must name one thing precisely.

Related: #5214 (the six small packages, where this was found), #5357 (app-shell), #4538 (the original analysis).
